records.name_note: Admissible sources split on the name. NC State's dedicated page is headed Strobilanthes auriculata var. dyeriana and lists Strobilanthes dyeriana under Previously known as; RHS's dedicated page is headed Strobilanthes dyeriana with Name Status Correct. The bare binomial Strobilanthes dyeriana (RHS) is recorded as accepted. On common name, RHS shows Persian shield as the common name under its heading, with royal purple plant under Other common names; NC State's description opens with Persian Shield, and its Common Name(s) list runs Burmuda coneflower, Persian Shield, Royal Purple Plant in alphabetical order.
unknowns: MoBot (plantfinder.mobot.org / www.missouribotanicalgarden.org) page for Strobilanthes dyerianus (kempercode a122) was found by search but would not load in this session (TLS/connect failure), so no MoBot content is used; MoBot would likely supply water, humidity, pH, toxicity and size fields. No UF/IFAS, Clemson, Penn State, UMD or UGA dedicated page for this taxon was found; only multi-species pages surfaced, which were not used.
toxic_to_pets, toxicity_detail, is_edible, attracts_pollinators: neither the NC State page (no Poison, Problem-for-Cats/Dogs or Attracts fields) nor the RHS page addresses them; left null.

chill_damage_f and temperature ranges: NC State gives only a frost tender tag, a 'not an evergreen in locations that experience frost' remark and zones 8b-11b, which are hardiness ratings, not damage-onset temperatures; RHS gives only the shared hardiness legend plus H1B. Left null.
humidity_need: NC State carries humidity tolerant / high humidity tags and Resistance To Challenges: Humidity, which describe tolerance, not a need; left null.
water_regime and watering fields: no admissible dedicated-page watering statement; NC State only says to provide good drainage and RHS gives only Moisture: Well-drained. Left null.

soil_drainage: NC State gives bare Good Drainage with no moisture pairing and RHS gives bare Well-drained, so ambiguous; null. soil_base: NC State says High Organic Matter and rich soil, RHS's Cultivation text is genus-style under-glass advice; null.
soil_ph: NC State lists Acid (<6.0) and Neutral (6.0-8.0), both bands open-ended or closed-top, and RHS lists Acid or Alkaline or Neutral, so no floor or ceiling is set.

outdoor_sun_exposure: NC State's structured Light field gives Dappled Sunlight and Partial Shade, mapped to part_shade. RHS Position lists Full sun and Partial shade; full_sun is omitted because NC State's North American structured Light field excludes it. NC State prose also says bright light with no direct sunlight, which conflicts with RHS, so direct_sun_hours_max is left null.

Size: NC State's dimensions (Height 3-4 ft = 36-48 in, Width 2-3 ft = 24-36 in) are used as the anchor. RHS gives Max Height 0.5-1 metres (19.7-39.4 in) and Max Spread 0.5-1 metres (19.7-39.4 in) over 5-10 years, a different range; disclosed, not used.
scientific_name_accepted: sources disagree on rank. NC State treats it as Strobilanthes auriculata var. dyeriana (not a bare binomial); RHS accepts Strobilanthes dyeriana, which is what is recorded.
fertilize and light_fc fields: no admissible species-specific figures; null.

RHS's Name Status row for Strobilanthes dyeriana reads Correct; it is not cited, because the bare one-word value evidences nothing alone. The accepted name rests on RHS's dedicated page, headed Strobilanthes dyeriana, and on NC State listing Strobilanthes dyeriana under Previously known as for its Strobilanthes auriculata var. dyeriana page; the rank disagreement is disclosed in name_note.

NC State's Common Name(s) list is alphabetized and shows Haage Zinnia then Mexican Zinnia, and its description opens "Haage zinnia, or Mexican zinnia". Haage Zinnia is used as the lead name. records.toxicity_detail: NC State's page carries no Poison block; its Tags row reads "#low maintenance #drought tolerant #deer resistant #heat tolerant #non-toxic for cats #non-toxic for horses #non-toxic for dogs #groundcover #native annual #wilson mg plant sale 2021 #pest resistant #easy to grow #pollinator plant #container plant #hummingbird friendly #bee friendly #mass planting #butterfly friendly #slopes #annual #patio #walkway #long bloom season". toxic_to_pets is false on the explicit #non-toxic for cats and #non-toxic for dogs tags (the page also tags it non-toxic for horses). There is no symptom list, no poison-part list, no toxic principle and no handling warning, so no human-toxicity severity is available. These tags come from NC State only; no other admissible source addresses toxicity for this exact species.

toxic_to_pets, toxicity_detail: the NC State page for this species carries no Poison block and no Problem for Cats/Dogs tags, and no other admissible species page was read, so toxicity is unknown, not safe.
is_edible: no admissible source read addresses eating this plant; left null.
chill_damage_f: NC State says only that it 'is sensitive to cool temperatures' with no onset figure. Its USDA zone list (9a through 12b) is a hardiness range, not a damage threshold. Left null.
water_regime and all watering fields: NC State gives only the soil adjective Moist plus 'If indoors, place in a sunny location and reduce watering', which is not a watering regime. Left null.
soil_drainage is moderate from NC State's structured Good Drainage plus Moist pair and its 'well-drained moist soils' prose. No source describes sharp or sandy drainage, so it is not fast.
soil_base garden_bed is taken from the 'When planted outside' prose. NC State also lists container, hanging basket and houseplant uses, and gives no potting-mix advice.

outdoor_sun_exposure: the structured Light field lists Full sun and Partial Shade; Partial Shade is mapped to part_shade. NC State's prose frames shade as a tolerance ('It will tolerate hot summers and partial shade and does well along a border or pathways.') and its tags include '#partial shade tolerant', while its preference is 'When planted outside, it does best in well-drained moist soils in full sun.' No second structured sun field was reachable to confirm or exclude part_shade. The '2-6 hours' wording is the site-wide category legend, so direct_sun_hours_max is left null.

Size: the structured dimensions (height 18-30 in, width 24-36 in) are the anchor. The same page's prose says it may reach 2 to 3 feet tall in its native habitat and 12 to 18 inches tall with a similar spread as an annual.
Not set from this page: humidity, light in footcandles, day and night temperatures, soil pH, fertilizer.
Sibling and hybrid pages were not used. NC State lists Cuphea hyssopifolia and Cuphea ignea only as plants that fill a similar niche; no 'Vienco' or 'Tiny Mice' hybrid page was cited.

records.name_note: NC State's dedicated page for this hybrid is headed "Mimulus x hybridus" (Monkey Flower is its only listed common name) and files it under genus Mimulus; this was not checked against Erythranthe × hybrida, because no admissible source with a dedicated page for Erythranthe × hybrida, and no RHS name-status entry, was found. Monkey Flower is a genus-wide name, but the hybrid's own page offers no more specific lead, so it is used here. The native Mimulus ringens is already in this catalog under its own dedicated-page lead, Allegheny Monkey Flower; the two records are distinct species and are kept distinct by name and binomial.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State's Ethnobotany block on the dedicated page says: "The leaves can be eaten raw or cooked. They have a slightly bitter flavour and are mostly added to salads as the leaves can also be used as a lettuce substitute. Native Americans ate the young stems and leaves of smaller, non-woody varieties." The page carries no Poison block and no Problem-for-Cats/Dogs tags, so no pet-toxicity or human-toxicity information was found. The page is an annual (Plant Type: Annual).
unknowns: Only one admissible source with a dedicated page for this exact hybrid was found: NC State. RHS, Missouri Botanical Garden, Clemson, UF/IFAS, Penn State, UMD and UGA pages for Mimulus x hybridus were not located; searches returned only other Mimulus species and cultivars, which were not used.
Whether Erythranthe × hybrida is the accepted name is unverified; scientific_name_accepted just repeats the name NC State's dedicated page uses and no RHS Name Status was found.

toxic_to_pets left null: the NC State page has no Poison block and no Problem-for-Cats/Dogs tags. Edibility (leaves eaten raw or cooked, young stems and leaves) comes from NC State's Ethnobotany block with no stated preparation times or conditions; no toxicity statement was found to weigh against it.

soil_drainage moderate is read from NC State's Soil Drainage tags Good Drainage and Occasionally Wet plus the description's 'moist, well-drained soil'; moisture_retentive was not set because no source states it as a requirement.
water_regime keep_moist rests on NC State's description sentence that the soil needs to be kept well-watered; there is no numeric interval or dry-down target.

NC State states 'Does best with cool night temperatures' but gives no temperature numbers, so day/night temperature fields are null. The Partial Shade tag includes a generic 2-6 hours legend, not used for direct_sun_hours_max.

NC State gives 'Available Space To Plant: Less than 12 inches' and no Dimensions block, so mature height and spread are null. No pH, humidity, light foot-candle, fertilizer or pollinator data on the page.
is_houseplant true rests only on NC State's Landscape Location list, which includes Houseplants alongside Container and Hanging Baskets; the page describes the plant as a showy annual.

records.name_note: Missouri Botanical Garden's dedicated Diascia barberae page leads with 'Common Name: twinspur', and its prose reads 'Diascia barberae, commonly called twinspur'. NC State's dedicated page renders a Common Name(s) list of Barber's Diascia then Twinspur, and its description text calls the plant Twinspur ('Twinspur is a mat-forming perennial from southern Africa'). Twinspur was chosen as MoBot's lead name and the name both sources' prose uses. Barber's Diascia is NC State's first-listed alternate.
unknowns: toxic_to_pets, toxicity_detail left null: neither NC State nor MoBot page carries a poison or pet-toxicity field for this species.
is_edible left null: no admissible source addresses eating this plant.

is_houseplant false: sources describe it as a garden, container and hanging-basket plant grown as perennial or annual (NC State Landscape Location: Container, Hanging Baskets, Rock Wall, Walkways; USDA zones 8a-11b); no admissible source gives indoor culture.

water_regime left null: MoBot's culture text says 'consistently moist, well-drained soils' (a soil description) while MoBot's structured Water field is Medium; no watering statement found. NC State likewise gives only soil drainage/moisture tags.
soil_base left null: no source states a potting-mix type; NC State lists High Organic Matter soil texture.
soil_ph_max left null: NC State's 'Neutral (6.0-8.0)' band is the only pH data and no RHS species page was available to check a ceiling against; min 6.0 taken from the band's closed lower edge.
humidity_need low rests on NC State prose 'They do best in climates with lower humidity.'; no numeric humidity range given.
No RHS page for D. barberae itself was found (search returned only cultivar pages), so RHS was not used. Clemson/UF/other listed hosts returned no dedicated page or were not reachable.

MoBot page was read through the browser pane because the script fetcher cannot reach plantfinder.mobot.org; its structured height is 0.75 to 1.00 feet and spread 1.00 to 1.50 feet, but only the prose single figures (12 in, 18 in) were used, so mature min fields are null.

Temperature, light fc, fertilizer, chill damage and watering interval fields have no admissible support and are null. MoBot hardiness zone 8 to 11 and NC State zones 8a-11b are survival ratings, not damage-onset temperatures.

outdoor_sun_exposure is full_sun only. NC State's structured Light field lists 'Full sun (6 or more hours of direct sunlight a day)' and 'Partial Shade (Direct sunlight only part of the day, 2-6 hours)', its tags read '#full sun tolerant' and '#partial shade tolerant', and its prose says 'Twinspur prefers moist, organically rich, well drained soils and blooms best in full to part sun.' records.toxicity_detail: NC State's Tags line for Felicia amelloides reads: "#blue flowers #daisy-like #tender perennial #non-toxic for cats #non-toxic for horses #non-toxic for dogs #annual #subshrub #bushy #groundcover". It tags the plant non-toxic for cats and non-toxic for dogs (and horses). The page has no Poison block and no handwashing or handling warning, and no other admissible source was reachable to confirm or contradict this.
unknowns: Only one admissible source was usable: the NC State Plant Toolbox page for Felicia amelloides. The RHS page could not be found (the guessed URLs returned 404 or a generic search shell, and the RHS search page is JavaScript-rendered, so no species page URL was discoverable). MoBot (www.missouribotanicalgarden.org and plantfinder.mobot.org) failed to connect (ConnectError), EDIS search returned no species page, and Clemson returned 403. Every null field is null for lack of admissible-source support.

scientific_name_accepted comes from the NC State page binomial; RHS Name Status was not checked, and the page's 'Previously known as' list (Aster amelloides, Aster capensis, Aster coelestis, Felicia aethiopica) was not used for a name decision.

The contrast with Argyranthemum frutescens (marguerite daisy) was not documented, because no admissible page for that taxon was fetched. Blue Marguerite appears in the NC State name list for F. amelloides, and the record covers F. amelloides only.

water_regime left null: NC State says 'average, consistently moist, well-drained soils', which describes the soil and is not a watering instruction. The same page says these plants 'do not tolerate wet soils' and that root rot may occur in wet soils. No structured moisture field is on the page.
soil_drainage is moderate (moist but well-drained); the same-source wet-soil and root-rot warnings rule out moisture_retentive, and the page does not say sharp or sandy drainage, so not fast.

outdoor_sun_exposure is full_sun from NC State's prose 'grows best in full sun'. The page has no structured light fields, so part_sun and part_shade are not supported. The page also notes flowering declines or stops by mid-summer in hot southern summers and that the plant does not tolerate hot, humid summers.

No NC State Poison block, temperature tolerance, humidity, pH or fertilizer information appears on the page. The page gives USDA zones 10a-11b and describes the plant as perennial in frost-free climates and otherwise grown as an annual. That is a hardiness rating, not a chill-damage onset temperature. is_houseplant is false: the page gives no indoor culture (its only indoor mention is starting seed indoors before the last frost), and its Landscape Location field lists Container, Hanging Baskets and Walkways with no Houseplants value.
is_edible is null because no admissible source addresses eating. Pollinator support is NC State's Attracts field (Butterflies) only.

is_edible is null: no admissible source addresses eating this plant.

is_houseplant false: NC State describes container, hanging-basket and ground-cover use and says it is grown as an annual north of USDA zone 10, but never calls it a houseplant or gives indoor culture; its Landscape Location field lists Container, Hanging Baskets and Rock Wall with no Houseplants value.

chill_damage_f is null: NC State says only that it does not tolerate winter cold and lists USDA zones 10a-12b, which are a hardiness rating and not a damage-onset temperature. The page also says it dislikes hot summer temperatures and may stop blooming at high night temperatures, but gives no figures, so day and night temperatures are null.
soil_base is null: NC State gives only 'light, well-drained soil' with Loam (Silt) and Sand textures and gives no potting-mix recommendation, and the page lists both container and in-ground uses.

soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max are null: NC State's Soil pH values are Alkaline (>8.0) and Neutral (6.0-8.0), with no Acid band. RHS's dedicated profile gives pH 'Acid or Alkaline or Neutral', so the 6.0 bottom of NC State's neutral band is not a floor. The alkaline band is open-ended, so there is no ceiling.

outdoor_sun_exposure comes from NC State's structured Light values 'Full sun' and 'Partial Shade'. NC State's prose qualifies the shade: 'Plant in full sun to encourage blossoms and in light, well-drained soil. In hot climates, it will accept partial shade in the afternoons.' RHS's (UK) Position field lists Full sun only. direct_sun_hours_max is null because the only hour ranges on the page are in the generic light-category legend.

water_regime follows the species prose 'Provide even moisture and allow the top of the soil to dry before rewatering'. The same page says watering is finicky: too much or too little can cause foliage drop or root rot. It also lists Drought under Resistance To Challenges, which is not used as a watering instruction. Day intervals, check depth and fertilizing are not stated, so they are null.

The NC State Plant Type tags are Annual, Ground Cover, Herbaceous Perennial and Vine. The description calls the plant a 'trailing, tender, herbaceous perennial vine or sub shrub'. The description says it will grow to about 9 inches high but spreads to 3 feet, which matches the Dimensions block.
NC State notes that the plant is thought to be extinct in the wild (it is also tagged #endangered). This is a conservation status and is not used for any care field.
